scope: Independent review of A104 original-byte predicate, write and subsequent read under synthetic MMIO; physical register semantics remain unproven.
checks: Independently decoded the exact 56-byte A104..A13C body from the pinned firmware. Its predicate matches A148: R0==1 and unsigned R1<=1, or UXTB(R0-2)<=1 and R1==0.

The accepted path builds 0x8000FF00 | ((R0<<6)&0xFF) | (R1&0x3F), stores one word at 0x40010000, performs one later fresh word load from the address register, ignores that loaded value, and returns zero. Rejection returns literal 0x004A0001 or 0x004A0002 without a store.
Reran all 54 original-byte fixtures in an isolated output directory; regenerated rows match exactly, including accepted low-byte aliases 258/259 only with R1 zero and rejection boundaries.
Accepted fixtures log exactly one 32-bit write and one following read at the same register; rejected fixtures have neither. The function has no helper calls or stack frame, and SP is unchanged.
limitations: The memory-mapped register is synthetic. The instruction trace does not establish command meaning, peripheral side effects, or actual hardware readback behavior.
Only the supplied finite test matrix is covered; no broader runtime reachability or canonical coverage is implied.
